brief: Goldman's five 2027 outlook notes (macro, equities, credit, rates, FX, commodities) converge on one causal chain: global AI investment keeps rising, from $1.1 trillion in 2026 to $1.8 trillion in 2027, but its growth rate as a share of GDP peaks in 1H27, a second-derivative turn that threatens markets more than the economy, since AI explains only 21% of US GDP growth versus 62% of S&P earnings growth and up to 92% of US market-value gains. That asymmetry drives every asset call: S&P EPS growth more than halves (36% to 11%), with an S&P target of 8,700 and a recommendation to buy Hyperscalers at 19.7x; AI debt issuance widens credit spreads (IG 88bp to 105bp, HY 320bp to 410bp); bonds regain hedge value because AI, not oil, now drives stocks (10Y target 4.6%, versus a current yield above 5.15%); the Dollar, now AI-linked, is forecast to fall roughly 3% while the Yen and Yuan strengthen; and a collapsed oil risk premium argues for buying gold and copper as hedges. Goldman's baseline is benign, but the author argues the downside path is more likely, citing continued Fed hikes, record equity supply, and credit already cracking at the AI edges.
